With furred arms outstretched, the lexati glides from the mountain cliffs to skim over the wide open Wealdwoods canopy, a sunlit 
world untouched by the crawling competition and mayhem below. Skillfully snatching birds and large flying insects mid flight and 
feasting on the fruits of the highest branches. Unfortunately, a handful of predators can dispel this arboreal paradise with the gliding 
mammal often having to dodge the acidic streams of ynnil spittle or the claws of skyelarx and basilospri. Th ese amiable felines are often 
found in familial clowders playfully bounding along the tops of the trees. Th ough incapable of true flight, the lexati can rise to great 
heights by riding warm updrafts to nest in safer, harder to reach areas amongst communal roosts in the treetops or cliff face ledges.
Class - Mammalia • Genus Derived Evolution - Leopardus • Niche - Specialized Aerial Omnivore

Vaulted Jump Th e lexati can leap into the air 20 ft. and begin 
gliding. During this glide, it gains a flying speed of 40 ft., and 
can move 5 ft. horizontally for every 1 ft. it descends, and it can 
pass over other creatures and obstacles. 
Hooked Claws Melee Attack Roll: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. 
Hit: 5 (1d4+3) Slashing damage. If target is a Medium or smaller 
creature and the lexati glided a 20+ ft. straight toward the target 
immediately before the hit, the target takes an additional 4 (1d8) 
Slashing damage has the Prone condition.
Senses Darkvision 30 ft., Passive Perception 14
Challenge 1 (XP 200; PB 2)
Wary Instinct (1/Day) Once the lexati is engaged in combat. 
On its turn, Dexterity Saving Th row: DC 14, the lexati. Success: It 
Disengages from combat by leaping upwards and gliding away. 
Th e lexati doesn’t provoke an Opportunity Attack when it glides 
out of an enemy’s reach.
Skills Acrobatics +5, Perception +4, Stealth +5
Encountering To those Travelers with a penchant for climbing, 
these highly social and intelligent creatures often respond with 
curiosity when a new creature enters their aerial domain. Th ough 
the group will respond amiably to offerings of fruit, any form of 
aggression or violence to their kind will be communicated to the 
whole colony, having them flee on sight, or attack en mass.
Reactions
Feline Finesse Trigger: A creature the lexati can see hits it with 
an attack roll. Response - Dexterity Saving Th row: DC 15, the lexati.
Success: Th e attack misses instead.
With large eyes and sensitive ears, this feline has an 
incredible range of senses to sight prey over the distant tree 
tops as well as forage for fruit in the quieter, star filled nights
A long tufted tail grants the 
lexati maneuverability during 
distant glides as well as balance 
for precipitous climbs
The wide furred patagium membrane stretching 
from the fifth digit's distal phalanges to the torso 
allows the lexati long controlled glides to travel great 
distances above the tree tops of the Wealdwoods
